name: activity-log
title: Activity Log
description: Who changed what, and when, with undo: createActivityLog records the page's UI SDK control changes (from people, agents and the app) and the app's own records, and steps back and forward through them. ActivityLog lists them newest first; pressing an entry seeks to it, Undo and Redo bind Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z outside text fields, and undoToast shows a toast with Undo. Agents call undo, redo and seek; a seek that undoes more than confirmAbove entries needs a person (data-agent-confirm).
docs: Create the log once in the browser, with the app's agent bridge, before the controls render: `const log = createActivityLog(agent, { within, describe })`. Then `<ActivityLog log={log} label="Activity" header={…} />`. `log.record({ label, description, actor, undo, redo })` adds a change of the app's own, like a task an agent moved. `log.undo()`, `redo()`, `seek(n)` (0 is the start) and `undoActor("agent")` resolve with what they couldn't put back; restoring goes through the bridge, so permissions and change callbacks still apply, and a password, card or one-time-code field is never put back. It wraps UI SDK's experimental history helpers behind its own types. Entries read UI SDK's English sentences unless you pass `describe`; every label is overridable.
